lines.text: A tin box on the sill. The clasp has been tried.
A wall of ice right across the street, older than the rest of it. White, not clear, laid down in bands like years. Nothing has cut it, and it doesn't melt.
It won't take a word from me. It's waiting on some other word.
A wall of ice right across the street, older than the rest of it. White, not clear, laid down in bands like years. Nothing has cut it, and it doesn't melt.
Old ice, is it? I have played to colder rooms than this, Eldwin, and to harder faces, and once, God help me, to the Temperance Society. Stand back and let a professional work.
The ice lets go all at once, like a held breath. The street goes on.
Twice in one week. I could get used to being useful.
